A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, references, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original synthetic experiments with LSA and GPT-2 models, including test losses and task-selection probabilities.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, supplemented by Qwen reasoning results in Table 1 and task-selection simulations in Appendix B.1.

M1.justification: The proposed LSA model, test-time CoT recursion, and quadratic task-selection procedure remain unchanged. The Qwen experiments and newly documented GPT-2 implementation details do not establish a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Beyond v1's synthetic linear-regression tasks, Section 5.2 adds OMEGA GCD and polynomial-root reasoning as fine-tuning tasks, with evaluation on GCD. This substantially extends the represented tasks beyond synthetic weight prediction.

E2.justification: Appendix B.1 introduces direct comparisons of optimized task selection against uniform selection and uniform selection restricted to easy tasks. Section 5.2 adds the Qwen-Base, Qwen-GCD, and Qwen-Poly comparison. Neither comparative evaluation appears in v1.

E3.justification: New protocols include Qwen RL fine-tuning with GCD accuracy grouped by CoT character length, and task-selection simulations with training/test prompt lengths n=50 and m=500. For retained experiments, the reported GPT-2 budget changes from 20k to 25k steps, and LSA initialization changes from the Eq. (3.6) description to Theorem 3.1 with random V31 entries. These are reported setting changes, not evidence of reruns; Figure 2's caption still describes fixed initialization.

E4.justification: Appendix B.1 adds a focused analysis of whether optimized, uniform, or easy-only training mixtures prevent overthinking as generation length increases, extending v1's selection-probability analysis. Section 5.2 also contrasts matched and mismatched fine-tuning. The existing prompt-length and covariance-shift analyses remain.

E5.justification: The existing reporting of averages over 10 runs and GPT-2 standard-deviation error bars is retained. The added experiments introduce no new seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Table 1's parenthetical percentages describe data fractions, not uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds short/long-CoT GCD accuracies of 30.39/27.2% for Qwen-Base, 75/38.4% for Qwen-GCD, and 29/20.83% for Qwen-Poly. Figure 5 adds decreasing error under optimized selection versus eventual increases under uniform and easy-only selection. Figures 1–4 retain their results. The new prose's +44.69% short-CoT gain disagrees with Table 1, which implies 44.61 percentage points.

T1.justification: Before Eq. (4.2), v2 corrects the multi-task estimator by restoring the missing outer I minus operation in [I - (I - Gamma^-1 Sigma_hat)^k] w_test. This agrees with Eq. (A.9), already present in v1. The theorem statements and appendix proofs otherwise retain their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims about context-length/test-time-compute tradeoffs, insufficient skill coverage, covariance-based task hardness, and selecting diverse, relevant, hard tasks. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly interprets longer-CoT accuracy groups as evidence of harder examples and of beneficial versus harmful thinking under aligned versus misaligned training. Appendix B.1 interprets optimized selection as preventing overthinking. The stated limitations to linear regression and single-layer LSA theory remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents the GPT-2 output projection, curriculum learning, equal training/test prompt lengths for Figure 2, and the precise LSA initialization distribution. It also specifies the Qwen model and the new simulation's prompt lengths. These expand reproducibility information, although detailed RL settings remain absent.

R1.justification: V2 adds Sun et al. (2025) as the OMEGA reference. The earlier cited works and substantive positioning relative to prior transformer and test-time-scaling research remain; the widespread citation-format change is presentational.

P1.justification: V2 adds Sections 5.2 and B.1, moves references after the appendices, switches to author-date citations, and makes local wording and acknowledgment edits. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 1 and Figure 5, rearranges Figure 2 from three panels above one to a two-by-two grid, and resizes or repositions Figures 1 and 3. Figure 2's caption gains a prompt-length clarification. The original plotted content remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new task-selection comparison supplies direct performance evidence where v1 showed selection probabilities, while the estimator correction and implementation disclosures improve clarity. However, Table 1's model-dependent CoT subsets do not isolate the effect of extra thinking, limiting the claimed real-reasoning validation. The revised LSA initialization text also conflicts with Figure 2's retained caption. These limitations keep the net quality gain modest.
